This function-local L1->L3 import is RETAINED after walking ADR-006 Violation #11's three remedies and finding each one makes the guard it feeds strictly worse. It is a pre-existing import, not a newly added apologetic one: ADR-006 Phase 5 forbids reaching for a lazy import as the ROUTINE answer to a new cross-layer need, and the finding here is the residual left after that protocol is applied honestly.

WHAT THE IMPORT BUYS. _declared_emitted_options is the read side of _reject_sensitive_plugin_env_placeholders_before_expansion, the pre-expansion guard that refuses a ${VAR} in any plugin option declared EmittedToOutput. get_shared_plugin_manager() calls register_builtin_plugins() on first invocation and publishes _shared_instance ONLY after that registration returns, so the declaration read cannot observe an under-populated registry. That self-triggering property IS the security control: the guard derives its forbidden-field set from the live plugin declarations at the moment it runs, and there is no window in which it can read an empty set and report success. In production code the only writer of _shared_instance is that initialiser (grep: manager.py:320 is the sole assignment outside the module's own declaration); the two test sites that monkeypatch it either install an already-registered PluginManager (tests/integration/web/test_execute_pipeline.py:458, which calls register_builtin_plugins() first) or reset it to None and restore (tests/unit/plugins/test_manager_singleton.py).

REMEDY 1 - 'move the needed code down' - BLOCKED, and blocked on honesty rather than effort. The manager cannot descend to core because its whole purpose is to discover and import the L3 plugin packages: register_builtin_plugins() delegates to plugins/infrastructure/discovery.py, which scans src/elspeth/plugins/**, and manager.py additionally imports plugins.infrastructure.hookspecs and plugins.infrastructure.validation (which itself imports plugins.infrastructure.config_base). Relocating the whole framework would move the SAME upward edge into discovery.py rather than remove it, and because discovery reaches the plugin tree through importlib on scanned paths rather than a static import statement, the relocated edge would become invisible to this rule while remaining a real core->plugins dependency. Shedding the finding by making the dependency unanalysable is precisely the move this burn-down forbids.

REMEDY 2 - 'extract the primitive portion and move that down' - BLOCKED, because the primitive is already down. The pure function (emitted_option_fields) and the marker (EmittedToOutput) live in contracts/emitted_option.py at L0 and core imports them at module scope today. What core needs from L3 is not a function but the registry's CONTENTS - the plugin classes whose get_config_model() carries the declarations - and those are the plugins themselves. There is nothing further to split off.

REMEDY 3 - 'restructure the caller so it does not need the cross-layer code' - BLOCKED, and it is the remedy that would actively reintroduce the defect this guard exists to close. Inverting the dependency means L3 pushes declarations into a core-owned registry at registration time and core reads it without importing plugins. That replaces a guarantee core can enforce (call the accessor, registration has happened) with an initialization-ordering assumption core cannot enforce, and the failure direction is SILENT PERMIT: a process that loads settings before or without registration reads an empty declaration set, forbids nothing, and reports success. That is the same fail-open shape as the hand-maintained {plugin: {field}} map this function replaced, which was a no-op for every plugin absent from it and is how truncate.suffix and csv.headers reached artifact bytes (elspeth-8f0a6b3391) and collectors went unwalked (elspeth-bc1b2c2959). Making the empty-registry read fail CLOSED does not rescue the inversion: the loaders that call this guard (load_settings, load_settings_from_config_dict) have 21 call sites in src/ and 240 in tests/, and the fix at each is to trigger plugin registration - i.e. to call into L3. One upward edge would become 261, distributed and forgettable.

SCOPE OF THE COUPLING. The import is function-local, so elspeth.core remains importable without elspeth.plugins and no module-scope cycle exists; the coupling is one registry read at settings-load time. What the value protects: an operator's host-environment secret being expanded into a CSV header cell, a report title, or a truncation suffix and written into an artifact a recipient can read. The declaration source is Tier-1 (ELSPETH's own plugin config models); the data being screened is Tier-2/3 operator- or web-authored YAML. The condition that would unblock the inversion is a declaration-harvest seam whose empty-registry contract is fail-closed AND whose registration trigger stays inside core's reach - proposed as follow-up on elspeth-f2c976264b, not attempted here. This and core/llm_profiles.py's provider-registry import are the only two L1 findings in the whole-tree raw corpus (3,679 findings at ff917243a); both are now rationalised on the same ground - core consuming a single authoritative L3 registry rather than maintaining a second, divergent copy of it.
